name: Pinkish Tan
lede: Pinkish Tan is a modifier-built name, "pinkish" plus "tan," traced to Robert Ridgway's 1912 Color Standards and Color Nomenclature.

sections.title: From Ridgway to the crowd
sections.body:
Our library traces this name to Robert Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature*, a book written for naturalists describing birds, mammals and plants [1]. The xkcd 2010 survey later recorded the same pairing of words independently [1]. The ISCC-NBS block for it reads "moderate yellowish pink" [1].

Its Munsell notation is close to 1.3YR 6.8/5.7, a warm, medium-light hue [1]. Close cousins in our library are [[tan|Tan]], [[blush|Blush]] and [[dusty-rose|Dusty Rose]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Pinkish Tan is comfortably common in our archive: it covers at least 2% of the canvas in 312 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed [2]. By its position in each painting's lightness order it is found in 156 of those, more common than 67% of the named colors we track, close to [[beige|Beige]] in that respect [2]. It most often plays an accent, the role in 48% of those paintings [2].

It peaks in paintings from the 1900s, at 1.6 times the archive's baseline rate, and is most over-represented in paintings from India, at 2.6 times expected [2]. Maurice Denis is its most devoted painter here, carrying it in 5 of his 43 works, 6.1 times his museums' baseline [2]. The earliest match is 1230, in a work by Berlinghiero, 682 years before Ridgway's 1912 record of the name, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
